Iteration 3 measures the ADR-020 skill (with_skill, 66b083d) against the SKILL.md shipped on main at 3e84241 (old_skill), one run per cell, four evals (eval 4 `end-leave` is new; eval 3's prompt now states the Goal is met so it measures `close`): with_skill 24/24, old_skill 22/24 (start-brief 6/7, end-leave 3/4). Tokens 128,520 vs 122,856 mean (+5,664, +4.6%); time 209.9 s vs 208.6 s.

The baseline is contaminated by design: only SKILL.md was swapped, while CLAUDE.md, docs/sessions/README.md, the skill's nested CLAUDE.md and the tool are the new ones. Three of four old_skill runs read those docs and followed the new procedure where it contradicted their skill — end-close ran `bun run session close` (a command its skill never names) and passed 6/6; start-brief declined to create a file, citing ADR-020; record-commit routed around its own injected `-- --check` line. The +0.10 delta therefore measures the SKILL.md text alone inside the new docs system, not old system vs new.

The two old_skill failures are both the join/none distinction the new skill makes explicit: start-brief's brief said `joined SES-004` while doing nothing on disk (SES-004's Goal is not this work — the grader applied the joined rule literally), and end-leave's closing note ran to 84 words against the 60 cap by repeating the handoff. with_skill said `none` on start-brief (correct: the message is a question) and 59 words on end-leave.

Harness state differed between clones: fixtures for start-brief and record-commit were cloned before 66b083d's entry commit (5476479) landed, so the tool appended a skeleton for 66b083d into whichever session the run targeted; end-close and end-leave fixtures were cloned after it and had nothing to sweep. All four affected runs (both arms of start-brief reported it as a finding; both arms of record-commit filled it from `git show`, flagged it as not made in this conversation, and named what they verified) handled it as the skill prescribes, and no expectation scores that handling.

The old skill's injected gate line `bun run session -- --check 2>&1 | tail -4` produced a stack-trace tail in every old_skill fixture: three sessions were open and the pre-fix tool threw instead of printing a refusal. Every old_skill run recognised it and ran `check --session SES-006` by hand. The tool now prints `session: 3 open sessions — say which with --session: …` and exits 1 (refuse(), uncommitted at the time of these runs); the new skill's injected line is `list`.

Verification of the fix's claim (record-commit expectation 3) was run in both arms — driver + swiftc in with_skill; driver + swiftc + a byte comparison in old_skill — and both updated all three stale docs; record-commit is 7/7 in both arms for the third iteration running and separates nothing.

Five graders independently flagged the same uncovered outcome for the third time: Outcome / Narrative / Shipped lines claim reads or reviews the transcript does not show (with_skill end-leave's Narrative claimed every session and CONTEXT.md were read; with_skill end-close's Outcome listed CONTEXT.md; old_skill end-close's Narrative asserted the prior review's reading order). No expectation ties those lines to transcript evidence; every run passed them.

Numeric handoff facts drift after the handoff commit: both end-leave arms wrote '3 commits ahead of origin/main' before committing, which made it 4. No expectation checks counts or shas in Open at end against HEAD.

Token cost per eval, with_skill vs old_skill: start-brief 169,367 vs 187,562; record-commit 139,565 vs 132,538; end-close 118,917 vs 82,094; end-leave 86,229 vs 89,228. The end-close gap is the with_skill run filling the swept-in 31-file skeleton (its fixture had it; the old_skill fixture did not) — harness, not skill.

Against iteration 2 (same skill text for the old_skill arm here as iteration 2's with_skill arm, but a different tool and docs): start-brief with_skill 129,909 → 169,367 tokens and 186.6 → 203.7 s; record-commit 92,712 → 139,565 and 202.4 → 277.0 s; end-close 89,627 → 118,917 and 179.6 → 206.5 s. Part of the growth is the swept-in skeleton in two of the three; part is the new skill reading every open session (three in these fixtures) rather than the newest.

One run per cell: iteration 2 measured 10–25% run-to-run spread on length alone, so the two-expectation gap between arms is at the edge of noise; what is not noise is that both old_skill misses are on the behaviours ADR-020 changed.
